lineage.rule: Excluded documents were fixed before inference and never replaced from reserve. Candidates must be compared on exactly these document-ID sets (the 999/1992 sets, not the nominal 1000/2000).

reserve_access_review.method: Reviewed every Bash/Write tool call of the M0 run that referenced the reserve files and their printed output.
findings: KLUE dev.tsv: only lines starting with '## klue-ner-' were read (ID header lines); output printed counts and hashes only.
KDPII test.json: json.load of the whole file, then only sent_idx was kept and the object deleted; output printed counts and hashes only.
No reserve sentence, label, prediction or score appears in any printed output, debug output or tool result.
reserve_access_review.conclusion: File accessed and structurally parsed; content not viewed, scored, selected or used. Independence of the reserve is still not claimed.
reserve_access_review.access_control_note: Presence under /tmp is not an access control. Experiment processes must be given development inputs only (the per-dataset ID lists), never the raw source files.

wording_corrections_applied.note: Original strings preserved here; replaced in the files because they overstated non-access.

klue_dev_reserve_2000.note: At M0 only header IDs were enumerated to compute the ID hash (a procedure the repository already uses). The pinned source file is one file and sits locally, hash-verified, but no reserve row was parsed or scored. Not independent (plan 3.1): auxiliary confirmation only, one opening.

kdpii_test_reserve_2391.note: The unmodified fetch script (shared with earlier runs) loads the whole test.json with a JSON parser to pick selected records, and this milestone read sent_idx of every row to hash the reserve ID list. No reserve label/sentence field was read, selected, converted or scored.

originals.baseline.reserve_unopened_confirmation: KLUE 2,000 and KDPII 2,391 reserve rows were not selected, parsed or scored.
originals.prereg.reserve_opening_policy.state_at_M: preserved unopened: no text, label or score viewed, none scored, none selected

mapping_finding.statement: The shipped name path maps only the E5 label private_person to KR_NAME (src/ko_pii_guard/ner.py). personal_handle is a separate E5 output class and is ignored by design.
mapping_finding.consequence: KDPII PS_NAME+PS_NICKNAME recall is low (kdpii_fresh_1992: 58.77% vs 82.50% for PS_NAME; the 34 nickname gold names add 1 TP) because nicknames are outside the mapped label set, not because they were tried and missed. Both policies stay in every report. Whether nicknames are required protection scope is a product decision and is not changed here.
